notes: Hanare kept as detached pavilion to mark the best room apart from the main house; leaf-boats kept literal for kiha-bune.

payload.english: The voice that joined the strings overbore the waters choking between the rocks and poured forth, with practised ease, a phrase in the Ikuta manner, and the guest, moved more deeply still, let his tobacco lie and looked up toward that quarter before he knew it. The shoji set its barrier between, and the pines, heedless, lodged shadows in the Kōrin manner. The guest turned his gaze as it was toward the valley below, yet as though his ear were still caught by the music he twirled his beard and did not stir. Like jewels spilling in disorder the hands on the koto quickened of a sudden, then flowed again, and after them rose a clear and gliding voice. The guest looked up toward that quarter once more.
notes: Ikuta is the Ikuta school of koto playing; Kōrin manner kept as in bible. 'Like jewels spilling' renders the image for the falling notes, not literal jewels.

payload.english: Stopping a maid who passed along the corridor and asking who it was that sang, he had her look him in the face and laugh in a strange way. Then she must indeed be some beauty. When he pressed her again, asking who, she would say only that she did not know, and already flushed to the brow she ran off toward the maids' room. No doubt to make a tale of it with one or another of her fellows. The guest smiled as he watched her go, then stepped out to the veranda edge above the water and leaned against a chair beside him. The player of the koto still sent forth a beautiful voice, unsparing.
notes: Kept singer and player ungendered to preserve the withholding: the Japanese gives only主. Oka-yaki rendered as flushing; tamari as maids' room.

payload.say: Drafted the first naming of Tatsuya and first appearance of Zenpei, keeping rank forms and Hotei bulk.

payload.english: The guest was a secretary in one of the ministries, Okumura Tatsuya by name, a man on the rise, who had begged official leave for an unexpected illness and, his health at last restored, had come this very day to the Umeya to nurse himself onward. His glittering dress and his splendid beard brought the master flying out from the front desk, and from under a reverent bow he was led to this detached chamber, richest of all in prospect. His face was that of a man of thirty or so, though it looked older still, and within his keen eyes there was an unaccountable amiability, which one of the maids, case hardened to guests, had found out, till it was on every mouth and made sport for her friends. Tatsuya was by nature quick to make himself at home, and in a moment he had become a gentleman with whom none need stand on ceremony. The master, who had lost his bearings before so lavish a tea money, hastily changed his dress and came out to pay his respects, and when he heard Secretary-sama he revered him only the more.
notes: Kept Japanese order Okumura Tatsuya on this first naming, and Secretary-sama with romanised suffix per bible to keep rank climbing visible. Kept tea money literal for the tip that unsettles the master. Kept beard as beard throughout.

payload.english: The koto presently brought its piece to an end, and quiet voices in talk within were faintly heard, uncertain. Tatsuya too was now gazing into the prospect spread before him, but his heart was already elsewhere. Just then a shoji opened with a rush, as if one within had risen to come out. Tatsuya's ear was quickest to catch it, and he turned. There at the rail stood one near fifty, full and round of face, at a glance a hale old man. Grown stout past all trace of bone, for all the world a Hotei, the squat laughing god, in a square sleeved robe, he turned with an amused face back toward the inside of the shoji, and at the tail of some word addressed to him bent his body back and laughed aloud. Of the one within, no shadow could be seen.
notes: Glossed Hotei once inline as the squat laughing god. Left the speaker inside the room unseen and the closing remark unattributed, as the Japanese leaves who speaks to whom to infer.

payload.say: Drafted p9-p11: Tatsuya's walk to Lake Ogi and first sight of the maiden.

payload.english: As if to mock him, Tatsuya left his chair, stepped down into the garden, and went out as he was to the riverbed to the east. Among the pines that crept across the earth, jumbled standing rocks had been hewn smooth and made, as nature offered, into seats to be seen here and there. The water that struck rock and broke on rock and pressed on white and blue entered into a thicket of green bamboo, and appeared again before a distant hill. The hanging bridge thrown across the stream laid black timbers over brushwood, and twined them about, uncertainly, with wisteria vines. Crossing the bridge, where the hill had been cut open, there was a little fall dropped as if without design. Climbing by a path left as it was, only just brushing aside the dew on the thorns, as if this were the way woodcutters should enter, halfway up, where pine and maple mingled their branches, there stood an arbour, clean to the very sight. The mountains opened of a sudden, and Lake Ogi, like a mirror, lay before his eyes.
notes: First clause keeps the Japanese as it stands: the laugh within is heard as mocking him, without naming who mocks.

payload.english: Spreading a round straw mat, Tatsuya rested his body, so soon wearied after his illness. The single block of the Umeya that faced him, with the mountain behind and the water before, was built with a care that was very fine. Chancing to fix his eyes upon that room on the second floor, Tatsuya perceived something more. Leaning against the thrown-open shoji stood a maiden, turned this way. She must be the mistress of the singing, Tatsuya thought at once.
notes: Round straw mat renders enzа, the woven seat laid out in the arbour. Mistress keeps the inference: he guesses the singer from the voice, as the Japanese leaves it.

payload.english: Her face could not be well seen for the distance, but the long pale face was surpassingly white, and her slender standing form was the more worth seeing. Idly looking up this way, as if startled to find one gazing hard at her, she hastily hid herself within the room. Tatsuya at last went down his way.

payload.say: Drafted p12-p14 keeping the lush bath-corridor gaze and Hotei echo.

payload.english: Though the days at a spa are long, noon had come at last. Having finished the two or three newspapers that had just arrived, Tatsuya had changed into the inn yukata to go to the bath and had stepped out into the broad corridor of the main house, when coming from the opposite way toward the foot of the stairs, passing him by, was one wiping with a steaming wet towel a neck smooth-drawn as jade. It was the maiden. That is she, Tatsuya marked at once. As he had fancied, her figure was beautiful beyond measure. With no adorning, a hundred native graces took a deeper lustre from the colour after bathing, and the stray hairs touching her snow-warm cheeks were bewitching beyond telling. A single dimple faintly breaking, eyes full of feeling stirring they knew not how, a gentle bearing not to be passed over, and ah, Tatsuya stood a while unable to move.
notes: Kept the long lingering inventory as one gathering sentence to preserve the lush erotic gaze; 玉を延べたる首筋 is a jeweled smoothness of the nape, rendered as smooth-drawn as jade rather than explained.

payload.english: Just then, towel in hand likewise, slowly coming down the stairs was that Hotei man he had seen a while before. The maiden, just starting up, looked back at him. "Oh Father, in again? Shameless, are you not," she laughed with a guiltless laugh. The sweetness of that smiling face was beyond words.
notes: Kept Hotei per bible for 布袋のその人; 幕なしねえ is girlish teasing at another bath, rendered as Shameless rather than literal curtain.

payload.english: "Father and daughter, first beauties of the land, Tokyo people," Tatsuya repeated in his breast as he went on to the bath. Coming after was master Hotei. Opening the right and left sliding doors of a bath newly fitted up at the upper end, the two went in together. At once was heard Tatsuya's voice, speaking to him without reserve.
notes: 国色 rendered as first beauties of the land to keep period height; 布袋殿 kept as master Hotei to hold the echo with p13.

payload.say: Drafted the bath parting, Tatsuya's untroubled counting of daughter and father, and the weather break into part two.

payload.english: Before long the two came out wrapped in the rising steam, already talking together with easy openness. Among spa people, quick to be friendly, Tatsuya was quickest at such things. As they parted for their rooms, master Hotei left this word behind, "Do come round a little to amuse me. I am at a loss with dullness." "To my side too, by all means," Tatsuya answered without lagging in courtesy, bending lightly at the waist.

Thus Tatsuya learned that Hotei was Miyoshi Zenpei by name, and in passing that his daughter was Mitsuyo, the youngest child and his treasured one. Miyoshi was a man of wealth he had heard tell of. Good. Very good indeed. For the days ahead to be idly spent, one more solace for the heart is one to the good. Beautiful prey. Puffing his cigar at ease, he thought after a while, and is not the rich man a fine thing too. Let this moment not be lost. He smiled to himself and breathed out smoke again.
notes: Kept 美しき獲物 as beautiful prey to hold the sporting appetite of the passage; left the Good, Very good reckoning as free thought without quotes so his tone does not darken, and kept cigar and smoke wording steady for the calculation motif.

payload.english: Clouds over the peaks flew chasing one another. Pines and far mountains were lost to sight. Rain coming. The voices of birds grew ever shriller.
Two

After half a day at go they had opened their hearts to each other, and Zenpei was above all delighted to have won Tatsuya. The few characters that read secretary of such a ministry, of such senior rank rang surpassingly well in old-fashioned ears, and to converse familiarly with such a man he counted as credit to himself, so no sooner visited than he returned the visit at once, wishing only to grow still closer. "He is a man of talent. A very considerable man of talent," he praised over and over, "and that absence of pride in him, that is grand. The interest of his talk. His pleasant way with people," admiring him point by point, till at last he muttered to himself that Tsunao and the like could in no way come up to him. Mitsuyo had been listening at his side, but "Even so, that Tsunao-san is younger and more refined, calm and high of spirit, and far, far nicer than that gentleman," she said with decision, pressing forward on her knees. "Ho, that was not for your ears." Zenpei broke into a laugh, and "Oh, I did not say it for any such reason. I only said it because it is so," she said, her face already tinged a faint pink, "horrid Father," untying and retying the cord of her sash.
notes: Mitsuyo calls Tsunao Tsunao-san with intimacy and Tatsuya ano kata, that gentleman, keeping a formal distance. I keep that contrast. Zenpei's hitori-gotsu is a mutter to himself, not addressed to her.

payload.english: "Speaking of Tsunao, he writes from his travels that he will stop here on his way home, and you must be glad of that," Zenpei began to tease, and "There you go again. I know nothing about it now," Mitsuyo said, whirling her back to him, angry in the way of a daughter.

Laughing, Zenpei went on, "But when Tsunao comes, the two of you will band together and set upon me, I suppose. To be lorded over still more than this I cannot bear. Shall I run away to Okumura-san's rooms? Thinking you have a backer behind you, you are grown quite bold," and gave her back a little prod with his pipe, and fell into a hahaha of solitary delight.
notes: gur[u] ni natte, literally of one belly, is conspiring or banding together. I render as band together to keep Zenpei's bluff tease without archaism.

payload.say: Drafted p22 to p24 as domestic comedy with Zenpei bluff and Mitsuyo wheedling kept intact.

payload.english: Mitsuyo turned back and looked into his face with an air of complaint. "Father, why do you favour Okumura-san so?" "Why? What do you mean by that? I praise him because he is worth praising," her father said, knocking out his tobacco. Her face took on a look of having something in mind. "But still, he is a stranger, is he not?" "Hm, I see. It vexes you that I do not favour Tsunao, is that it? Quite right, indeed it is. Oh, Tsunao is a splendid fellow. As you say, young and refined, and what was it now, yes, calm and high of spirit, and if you want still more, deep in learning and steady in hand and handsome and upright in conduct. Ah, I am worn out. A young man without a single fault to be found."
notes: "Steady in hand" renders 腕が確かで, taken as general competence rather than a particular skill; the weariness is Zenpei's comic piling-on, not a break in the list.

payload.english: "Say plenty of such things, do. When Tsunao-san comes I shall tell on you, so there. You really are a hateful Father," Mitsuyo said, sulking more than ever. "Dear me, I have spoilt your good temper," Zenpei said, drawing the air pillow beside him toward him and laying himself on his side. "I should like to show Tsunao just how you look like that," with a teasing face still.

"Very well. Tease me as long as you like. With you like that, Father, who knows how ill you speak even of me behind my back. From now on I shall not take a word you say as true, so there. You do not love me at all, Father. That is why the other day at home you slipped away from me and went to the play. I bear a great grudge, so there."
notes: Kept "take as true" for 真実にしない to hold the wording for her "truly, truly" outburst in p27 and Zenpei's mocking answer.

payload.say: Drafted p25 to p29 keeping Mitsuyo's sixfold truly and Zenpei's mocking echo intact.

payload.english: "My, how fearful. To be hated by you makes me sleepy," Zenpei said, closing his eyes as he was. "Oh, you must not go to sleep. I shall be lonely," Mitsuyo said, drawing near and shaking him. "Have you apologized, then?" he said, opening his eyes a slit. "I have nothing to apologize for. It is you, Father, who should apologize."

"Why, why?" Zenpei said, turning over onto his back, still letting a smile escape. "And yet, after tormenting me so much," Mitsuyo said, showing a little sharpness in her beautiful eyes. "What have I done to torment you? You are tormenting yourself alone. And indeed Tsunao is a fellow beyond compare."
"You speak of Tsunao-san again. Very well, Okumura-san is a splendid gentleman. I am truly, truly, truly, truly, truly, truly angry."
notes: Kept the sixfold repetition unvaried as in the Japanese. The first carries ruby honto, the rest shinjitsu, but the effect depends on sameness, so one English word throughout.

payload.english: "Ha ha ha ha. So greatly 'truly' angry. There is no need to announce each anger one by one. Since you are angry truly, shall I laugh lies, lies, lies?"
notes: Kept Zenpei's threefold uso ni parallel to Mitsuyo's truly, and kept truly in quotation marks as he mocks her word back.

payload.english: "Do as you please. I... I... I am going home. I shall go home and tell Mother of this and have her avenge me. Tsunao-san and I have been passed over for Okumura-san. I want none of them now, neither the yuzen silk you had made for me the other day, nor that gold hairpin, nor sash, nor ring, nothing. Give them all, just as they are, to Okumura-san. That haori of yours you told me to have tailored and left at home as it was, I shall cut it wrong on purpose and leave it full of flaws, so there. And that Ninsei incense box you gave me before, saying my tea practice had improved, I shall dash against a stone and break it, so there."
notes: yuzen is dyed kimono silk, haori a jacket worn over kimono, Ninsei the noted Kyoto ware; left in compact English form to keep the tantrum pace.

payload.english: Zenpei paid it no mind at all, gazing at the ceiling with a beaming smile. "Ah, Tsunao is a truly splendid fellow."

"Again, again. Father, really." Mitsuyo rose to her feet and with a sudden backhand snatched the air pillow away, so that Zenpei's head dropped with a thump. "Oh, what a cruel thing to do," he said, wincing into a smile. "Serves you right!" Having seized it for good, Mitsuyo pulled out the stopper and with both hands had already squashed it half flat.
notes: The Japanese here says only pillow, but it is the air pillow brought in two paragraphs before; the stopper would otherwise make no sense, so the English names it.

payload.english: Left with no choice, Zenpei sat up. "Then shall I make tea to make peace? Bring out those dried sweets we brought." "I know nothing about that," Mitsuyo said, still ruffled, rising with the folded pillow in her arms. "I think I shall go to the bath." "Do not say that. Come, bring them out," he coaxed from below, whereupon, seizing her moment to strike a pose, she drew herself up haughtily. "I am going to the bath. Ask Okumura-san to bring them out for you."
Three

"Out for a walk?" It was Tatsuya, calling from behind. Mitsuyo started and looked back, and finding no way to slip off made her greeting prettily enough. "Is it not a fine view? Have you been down toward the lake yet?" he asked. "No, not yet. I have only just left the inn," she answered self-consciously, the words not coming smoothly and her face bowing of itself. "Then come with me and let us walk a little about. My spirits are clear today, and it is just the weather ordered for a stroll. Your father went out somewhere a while ago, did he not?" in his usual light tone.
notes: The speakers are left to inference in the Japanese; the English assigns the questions about the view and the lake to Tatsuya and the self-conscious answer to Mitsuyo, as the scene requires.

payload.say: Drafted the walk invitation and lakeside passage with coaxing dialogue and unpruned scenery.

payload.english: "But Father will worry when he comes back, so I cannot go too far," said Mitsuyo, restless on her feet. "Why, from your room the whole of this ground is in sight. And you have me to attend you, though I grant I am a rather doubtful escort, but I mean to give you nothing to trouble yourself about. If you dislike it, however, there is no help for it."
notes: Mitsuyo's first line uses chichi for her father; Tatsuya answers in his usual light coaxing without pause for speaker tags in the Japanese.

payload.english: She could hardly say outright that she disliked it, and hung back. Tatsuya saw her unwillingness and went on lightly, "If I go plodding about alone I am soon weary and dull, and just as I was wishing for company you came here, that is your fate. It may trouble you, but do keep me company a little. In return I will grant you whatever unreasonable thing you ask," he said familiarly.

Unable to refuse, Mitsuyo yielded at last. It was morning. The sky was clear as if its depth had been turned outward, the white clouds of the peaks with nowhere to go, the snow lingering on the high ridges all the more vivid, piled indigo before and congealed ink behind, and as they went among swaying pampas grass and wild chrysanthemums and valerian, the stones grew ever thicker and the pines ever finer, and the glittering face of the lake met their eyes at once.
notes: Kept the kanbun-coloured landscape phrases piled indigo and congealed ink as written rather than smoothing them into plain colour words.

payload.english: Bent on winning her goodwill at every step, Tatsuya chose of set purpose to take the innocent part. From idle gossip of the world he passed to amusing things in fashion, leapt to the theatre and went to music, and spared no pains of every kind. Mitsuyo gave only answering replies, and never opened her mouth of herself.

payload.say: Drafted the lakeside turn from coaxing talk to lush tableau to silent walk back.

payload.english: "Shall I confess something odd?" Tatsuya said, smiling. "Apart from that time at Nasuno, how many times do you suppose I have heard your koto?" "There you go again," Mitsuyo said, stepping on ahead as if to escape, "oh, but just look. Have we not come to a fine view? That island is quite beyond words. Oh, how lovely!" And with that she made an end of the talk.
notes: I kept "that time at Nasuno" literal; the passage gives no more context for what hearing is meant, so I did not explain it.

payload.english: The famed reeds grew thick and close in their narrow place, and the wind in their upper leaves broke the ripples that came softly beating in. This was the strand of the lake. The peaks that stood in rivalry drowned their shadows whole, and a rowing boat far off pushed its way on across them. Pine islet and sundered rock, mountains shutting out the world and water clear for ever, fishermen's chants and water-chestnut songs, smoke-waves fading far, and the sky more vast still. Mitsuyo set herself upon a fallen tree and rested a while. The wind struck her powder and bore its bewitching scent to Tatsuya.
notes: "Ogi" names both the lake and the reed; I read the famed ogi here as the plant, not the place, but leave the echo audible. I kept the paired Chinese phrases as plain images rather than smoothing them away.

payload.english: "Let us go on. Father will be coming home by now," Mitsuyo said, rising. "There is nowhere here to rest at ease, and that is a pity," Tatsuya said, and left it to another time. Along the way Tatsuya spoke to her of one thing and another, but Mitsuyo gave only perfunctory answers and seemed to pay him no heed. Tatsuya too was plainly put out, and looked for all the world sunk in thought. The two walked on in silence.

At Mitsuyo's cry of "Oh!" Tatsuya lifted his downcast face, and saw Zenpei coming toward them with a strange man making straight for where they stood. "Tsunao-sama!" Mitsuyo cried, her face all at once alive, and ran straight toward him, saying as she ran, "When did you ever get here! You cannot know how I have waited! While you stayed away, Father did nothing but torment me." With a soft, cajoling glance at her father — "Father, I shall not lose to you now!" — she turned again to Tsunao, laughing: "Why did you not come sooner? It is too cruel. You care nothing for me, and that is horrid. And you have grown such a nasty beard—" She had got so far when, catching sight of Tatsuya's thick black beard as he came up beside her, she turned back in a flash: "Oh, forgive me! O-ho-ho-ho!" — her manner changed in an instant.
notes: Both hige terms here — Mitsuyo's tease at Tsunao and Tatsuya's black beard — use the same word 'beard' to keep the comic trip the Japanese sets up; her apology is aimed at Tatsuya.

payload.english: Presented by Zenpei as "a kinsman of mine, Tojo Tsunao," Tatsuya greeted him with his usual free and easy civility, but inwardly he was far from calm. Who was this pale, close-looking, queer fellow? And what to make of Mitsuyo's behavior? "Or perhaps—" the suspicion came, but he let nothing show and kept a cheerful face to the last. Though Tsunao handled him with a haughtiness that seemed to brush him from the tip of his nose, and stung him again and again, Tatsuya, a man used to people, let it pass with an easy laugh; Tsunao showed no sign of meeting him, and without so much as a glance said, "Mitsuyo, I have brought you a keepsake. What do you think it is? Guess."
notes: Tatsuya's 'Or perhaps—' leaves the inference unfinished as in the Japanese; the speaker of the keepsake line is Tsunao, addressing Mitsuyo only.

payload.say: Drafted p44 to p47 keeping the paired contempt, Zenpei's pleased misunderstanding, and the childlike run home intact.

payload.english: Zenpei stood alone between them, bent on making the two men friends. Hearing the word secretary, Tsunao looked down on Tatsuya as a poor wretch adrift on the waves of the world; hearing the words a graduate of last year in philosophy, Tatsuya laughed to himself at a fool ready to bury a lifetime in the most roundabout empty theory. Zenpei, innocent to the last, took it for certain that they had conceived a respect for each other, and chuckled to himself with delight. "Do show me the keepsake quickly," Mitsuyo said, as if coaxing him.

"We cannot talk at ease here. Shall we go back to the inn and drink a cup together?" Zenpei proposed. "Most excellent," Tatsuya answered on the instant. Zenpei turned. "Tsunao, come along." Tsunao, coldly: "Yes, let us go."

Each with his own thoughts, the four set out. "I shall run ahead for the keepsake," Mitsuyo said, throwing away the wild flowers she had plucked, and ran off like a child. Her skirts fluttering, white chasing scarlet. "Welcome back," came the chorus of voices from the Umeya.
notes: The line on hem, snow and scarlet is a brief lyrical flash with no verb; I have kept it as a visual fragment of white under-robe chasing red, rather than supplying weather or motive the Japanese leaves out.

payload.english: Four

payload.say: Drafted the waterside soliloquy in brisk ore voice, keeping repetitions and sporting delight intact.

payload.english: "That Tojo fellow, insolent to the last, who does not count me as a man at all." Tatsuya drained a glass of sobering water at a gulp, alone in his room, his eyes bright as he glared into space. What does he take me for, anyway? He never said it to my face, but he plainly insulted me. Just watch. Once I have him neatly in my hands I will smash him to powder. I am not the man to suck my thumb while another walks off with what I have marked. Once I have aimed I never let go. I saw plainly enough how he stands with Mitsuyo. To trample that self satisfied face underfoot will be as easy as breakfast. Does he know who I am? Does he know who I am? Ha ha ha ha, just like a scholar in his naivety. What a fool. Well, it looks as if I shall need a little strategy now. Splendid, splendid. Just when I was beginning to ache with too much quiet, a fine diversion has bubbled up. I will work it well and to the full. This is where my skill comes in. Well, things are getting interesting.
notes: The whole passage after the first sentence is soliloquy in coarse ore voice, against Tatsuya's polished public watashi. I kept it in vivid present and bluntly proprietorial, without making it brooding.

payload.english: Mitsuyo is only a peeping chick, after all. One blow to pinion her. I will give her no time to say yes or no. Still, a beauty like hers is not to be got elsewhere. I must treasure her for a start. The old man, the old man. I will never let him slip. Talk him round neatly, and my debts that I can never slip out of. Yes, that will do too and this will do too. Now, shall I lay my plot? The quicker the business the better. "Speed is everything in war." I will press hard on the chase and set to work at once. Good. Let me begin. Delay is loss. Hurry, hurry.
notes: The opening image is compressed in the Japanese, chick crying and wing clipping in one blow. I take it as contemptuous sporting language for an easy capture, and kept the bird figure rather than smoothing it away.

payload.english: Turning on his heel, he laid his hand on the electric bell by the pillar, and before he had time to wait one of the maids came running. "Look, go to Miyoshi-san's rooms and say this for me. I should like him to beat me at another game, and I have something else to talk of besides, so if he is free I would be glad if he would come at once. Hurry now, will you. Oh, your comb has fallen."
notes: The owner of the fallen comb is unstated; I take it as the maid's, dropped as she ran in, which fits Tatsuya's familiar notice of the maids.

payload.english: "That is mere obstinacy on your part. He is not a man to be cast aside like that. Whatever else, he is a man who has become a secretary. Bend a little and try keeping company with him." To Zenpei soothing him so, Tsunao only arched himself back and stayed stiff. "I have no thought whatever of mixing with such a man. Frivolous in looks, flippant, a man I dislike through and through. I hate even to see his face. I came here full of pleasure, and through that man I have met with nothing but disappointment. What good could come of company with such a creature. What is it in him that you find so much to your liking?"
notes: I read omae no ikkoku as obstinacy or prejudice on your part; the sense is plain from the reply but the wording is uncertain.

payload.english: "I do not like him either, somehow," said Mitsuyo, playing with her ring.

"Quite right. So it should be," said Tsunao, giving his pipe a tap. Even that sound grated on Zenpei's ears, and his laughing face clouded a little. "With any man, if you look you will surely find faults. Taking each other's good points and enjoying one another, that is what keeping company is. You grow more perverse by degrees. In that temper you will never push your way through the world." His voice, even so, was still mild.

payload.say: Drafted the inn quarrel through Zenpei's angry exit to Tatsuya's summons.

payload.english: "But what merit is there in that man? In the first place—" He was stopped before he could go on. "Enough. You may dislike him on your own reckoning. I shall keep company with him on mine, and we will say no more of this. That will do. There is nothing to be got by reddening our faces at each other." For all he said it, displeasure showed in his colour, and Tsunao held all the more stiffly to his own. "Still, if he were a stranger it would be another matter, but as it is you, I must tell you all that I believe. I must earnestly beg you to have done with him."
"Be silent!" The harsh voice burst out at last. "I will hear no more. What presumption."
"Oh Father, you are angry. Tsunao-san said it with no ill meaning. What a face you are making."
notes: Kept Mitsuyo's Tsunao-san with suffix as heard intimacy, against Zenpei's bluntness.

payload.english: "Nay, keep out of it. It is nothing you know of." Silenced by the unexpected volley, she had just closed her lips when a messenger from Tatsuya came in haste and delivered his message word for word as he had been told. Zenpei, half out of bravado, gave his assent with a ready answer and sent him back. Tsunao sat with folded arms and bowed head.
notes: Source has a missing or illegible character in 飛〓しり; read as unexpected broadside of anger falling on Mitsuyo.

payload.english: Mitsuyo looked anxiously from one to the other, and held back her father as he rose to go as he was. "Father, to part like this leaves an ill feeling on both sides, does it not? Do make your peace somehow before you go. It puts me in difficulty."

At the pretty meekness with which she bowed her head, Zenpei paused a moment and turned back. Tsunao did not unbend his grave face, but sat silent with knitted brows. To see it set his own heart ablaze too. 'Very well, leave him be!'
notes: Last sentence reads as Zenpei's unspoken flare rather than speech; set in single quotes as thought. Japanese leaves the subject of the burning heart unstated.

payload.english: Shaking off his sleeve, Zenpei went out with loud steps. Tsunao sank into himself and said not another word. All at once the water running through the valley struck upon the ear.

payload.say: Drafted p62 to p67 in Mitsuyo's wheedling voice against Tsunao's stiff refusal.

payload.english: "Tsunao-san, why do you dislike Okumura-sama so much? Could you not simply humour him and let it pass? Oh, do try to do so. When it comes to this I no longer know which side to take, and I truly feel like bursting into tears," Mitsuyo said earnestly. "If you can, do try to think better of it. Won't you?" she said, peering into his face. Her winning air was beyond telling.
notes: Kept honorifics as Tsunao-san and Okumura-sama to hold distance: she is intimate with him, distant from Tatsuya.

payload.english: Moved, Tsunao lifted his face and somewhat recovered his colour. Yet his words yielded nothing. "I cannot bend myself. That man displeases me through and through. I spoke from grounds of my own, but if Oji-sama will not make use of them, then that is that. And you, what do you think of the fellow?"
notes: Kept Oji-sama in romanised form rather than Uncle, since Tsunao's formal kin address matters and the bible asks for suffixes to stay.

payload.english: "I hardly know about such things, but a man who chatters so, I should think, can have little that is solid at bottom."
"Yes. Well said," Tsunao said with a trace of a smile. "You understand the better. A thing to admire." Plainly said, yet his face held tenderness.
"And, you know, there is something creepy about him. Perhaps it is only my fancy, but he is altogether strange."
notes: Kept bodily terms creepy and strange for kimi ga warui and hen, to leave her intuition bodily rather than reasoned.

payload.english: "Why is that?" Tsunao sent her a look, and she answered, with eyes that made her meaning speak, "Oh, it is nothing in particular, only, only, he is somehow queer. So I think I dislike him." "Hm," Tsunao said, as if with a cold smile, "with that fellow, it may well be so. Should he utter even a hint of such a thing, I will teach him shame to his heart's content. To fall prey to such a wretch would be a misfortune worse than death."
notes: Kept prey for ejiki to preserve echo with Tatsuya's utsukushiki emono in p16. The threat in katakoto demo... is left as Tsunao's resolve against any advance, though the Japanese leaves the exact occasion unsaid.

payload.say: Drafted the Tsunao and Mitsuyo farewell talk keeping her wheedling close and his stiffness intact.

payload.english: "When I think what may become of me I grow frightened, so while you are here, please, I beg you, stay beside me. When I think of such things I wish we might soon... oh..." She smiled shyly. "Well, let us stop."
notes: The sentence breaks off at 'hayaku nee... ano...': marriage is implied but not said, so the English leaves the break as it stands.

payload.english: "What are you saying?" Tsunao for the first time laughed clear and bright, but then, "I came all this way to come here, yet Uncle is as you see him, and that fellow will be coming in every day. The mere sight of him offends me, and there is no way for things to go on peacefully. I think I had best go home at once."
notes: Tsunao calls Zenpei 'Uncle' where Mitsuyo would say 'Father'; the English keeps Uncle to preserve the relation as spoken.

payload.english: "Oh, if you do such a thing it will seem all the more as if you are striking at Father, and besides, what is to become of me? To be left alone, it is hateful. If you go home, I shall go home with you."
"That will not do." Tsunao spoke firmly. "You must stay and nurse Uncle. You are still a daughter of the Miyoshi. Do you not hold Uncle dear? What foolishness to be in tears."
notes: 'Uncle' renders ojisama; Tsunao uses his own kin term for a man who is Mitsuyo's father.

payload.english: "Even so, I... You are too cruel." She had begun to bite the sleeve of her juban, then, "Then I shall beg Father, whether he will or no, for us all to go home together. Why have you so little feeling for me? You think nothing at all of me. You are glad to make me cry."

"You must not talk like that, it puts me in difficulty." Tsunao gave a wry smile. "Have no worry for what comes after. I shall without fail give Uncle a quiet word of warning. Nor do I myself wish to go home if I can help it."
"No, I will not let you go." Mitsuyo clung and coaxed.
notes: Kone mawasu is wheedling persistence rather than argument; the English keeps it physical and childish.

payload.say: Drafted the Tsunao and Mitsuyo parting quarrel through to the masseur closing the scene.

payload.english: "It is no use going on with such childish talk forever. We are to be parted again for a while, and will you show me such a face?"
notes: Speaker unstated; taken as Tsunao answering Mitsuyo in p74.

payload.english: "No, whatever you say, I will not let you go, and that is that."
Tsunao said nothing and hung his head. Mitsuyo drew close and peered into his face, laying her lovely hand upon his knee. "Do you so much want to go home?"
notes: Source prints the name as steel Tsunao here and in p78; normalised to Tsunao as in the rest of the text.

payload.english: Tsunao kept his lips shut and would not even look. "Then," Mitsuyo said innocently, bringing her face near, "will you take me with you? Eh? Do take me with you, will you?"
notes: Same name variant as p77; normalised to Tsunao.

payload.english: "Well, shall we both just go home?" Tsunao suddenly raised his head, and a tender light flashed in his eyes at the same moment, but in an instant he was himself again. "No, that will not do. You had better stay here."
"Oh dear, you say that again. Very well. Then I shall go home by myself."
From a room some way off came the thick voice of a provincial guest singing about trusting all to an ivy wig. In the passage a masseur sank to his knees with his "A treatment for you?"
notes: Song fragment left literal; sense of the lyric beyond the ivy wig phrase is unclear from this line alone.

payload.say: Drafted Tsunao's quiet departure and Zenpei's unknowing return.

payload.english: Tsunao would not bend, and in the end he went away. Leaving behind a single letter in which his brush had told his heart, with no farewell to Mitsuyo and none to Zenpei, he left the Umeya lightly, as if upon the wind. Clouds went and waters hastened, and his rickshaw left the sound of farewell in these hills, then vanished and was gone.
Five

It was Zenpei who came back, calling "Tsunao, Tsunao!" from outside the room in high spirits and a voice still gladder. Mitsuyo, tear-faced, sat drooping where she was and gave him no welcome. "What is it? What is wrong? Where has Tsunao gone?"

"Tsunao has gone home. Please look at this," Mitsuyo said, holding out the letter. Zenpei did not even take it in his hand. "What! Gone home in a temper, has he? The fool," and then, as if the rest were already forgotten, "That does not matter. Leave it be. Let him alone." He hastily drew the inkstone to him, dashed off three telegrams, called a maid and sent her off at once to post them, all but whipping her on her way, and without taking up his pipe or drinking his tea, his face flushed and his eyes fixed in one direction as if they gazed at something most diverting there, "A find, a find, this is a find indeed. With a secretary for a backer at one's back there is no question. Fellows like Tsunao cannot see a thing like this, and that is the trouble. The famous Kijima coal mine at any rate, two hundred thousand is a foolishly cheap price. Sold at a throwaway price it is still rated at five hundred thousand, the yearly output some hundreds of thousands, dividends so large as to be almost rare among coal mines, and the quality of the coal far surpassing even the coal of Miike, with sales for naval use at home and abroad of some hundreds of thousands of tons a year; why, the god of fortune has come to us from an unlooked for quarter. We must not let it slip to another. And Okumura is a worker. No course can come to a bad end," all as if no one stood before him.
notes: Kept the money figures vague as in the Japanese (twenty-man, fifty-man, yearly output in the hundreds of thousands) rather than tidying into exact sums; tons renders噸. Kept the triple 'find' repetition and the fixed gaze that looks past Mitsuyo.

payload.english: He knew that something had happened, though not what, and Mitsuyo, listless in herself and wanting comfort, resented a father who gave her none. Sorrow heaped with pique came to an ear, "Father, it is so dull, I shall go home too," she said, sullen and sharp with it. Zenpei scarcely took it in. "If that mine once comes into our hands, the smart I have suffered ever since that blunder over the shares will be quite cured. Besides, the losses the Sino-Japanese troubles brought upon our marine produce, this will make them good. I must bring it off well," he ran on, beside himself.
notes: 日清事件 rendered as Sino-Japanese troubles to keep the period phrasing; left as the cause of losses on marine produce exactly as the text gives it, without explanation.

payload.english: "Father, Father, I say, Father, I am going home," Mitsuyo raised her voice and spoke still more keenly. Zenpei, as if he marked her for the first time, "What, go home? I shall go home too. We must be back in Tokyo with all speed and settle this and that arrangement. Mitsuyo, we start early tomorrow. And that mine, I must have it at any cost," his heart already half gone ahead.

To have their starting fixed so lightly for the very next morning was more than Mitsuyo had looked for, and cheated of her scheme to tease him a little and trouble him and make him sullenly follow her will and so go home together, her maiden heart was displeased, displeased already at being made nothing of from the first, and she pressed close, "Father, is that truly so, eh, Father, do take it to heart and listen. You are too provoking. Father," till at last she pulled his ear. Zenpei, annoyed, "There, what a noise. Be silent. You disturb my thinking. Come, go and take a bath."
notes: 真実なの kept as truly to hold the echo with Mitsuyo's truly insistence in p27 and Zenpei's mocking answer; 父様 kept throughout as Father to hold her wheedling intimacy.

payload.say: Drafted p90 to p92 with Mitsuyo's sulk, the corridor meeting, and the cool departure kept plain.

payload.english: "Very well. Have it all your own way," Mitsuyo flung out after her usual manner, and turned away in a sulk. Zenpei, as though it were no concern of his, with the mine on his lips at every second word, his heart scarcely present in his body.

Rough upon the mats, venting herself upon the sliding doors, Mitsuyo went out of the room. Just then Tatsuya was passing along the corridor that leads to the main house. They met face to face, one above and one below, and Tatsuya smiled at her as he always did. Mitsuyo, her face set in a pout, turned her eyes away toward the ridge. Tatsuya smiled and passed on.
notes: I kept "one above and one below" as written, though the levels in the inn are not made clear; the point is a brief meeting and her turning away.

payload.english: As he had said, Zenpei hastened to leave while it was still early morning. Though shown no more tenderness today, Mitsuyo's face did not soften, yet her heart was already glad to be out of this house. Tatsuya came out to see them off. At sight of him Mitsuyo knit her brows and turned her face away. Tatsuya and Zenpei whispered together for a little, and ended laughing with one another. Mitsuyo pretended not to know and looked only elsewhere. At parting Tatsuya had one word: "Mitsuyo-san, when you meet Tsunao-san, please remember me kindly to him."
notes: "Remember me kindly to him" renders a set polite formula; I left its sting to context rather than stressing it.

payload.say: Drafted the Tokyo return and Tatsuya's smiling arrival.

payload.english: Six

With the shade of the woods at Ueno to greet her, Mitsuyo drew her first free breath. Without waiting for tomorrow she coaxed leave from her mother, and forgetting even her shyness in the thought, she went at once to Tsunao's lodgings; but alas, Tsunao had not yet come home, and as Mitsuyo turned back, crestfallen, the stray hairs she could not brush away were tossed by the autumn wind, which knows one's heart.
notes: Ueno woods marks the return to Tokyo after the spa; the closing image follows the Japanese in giving the wind, not Mitsuyo, the knowledge.

payload.english: Since coming home Zenpei had hardly warmed his seat, hastening east and running west, rushing about day after day as if possessed. Visitors arriving in parties of three and four shut themselves with him in one room and held long secret counsel. The busier the days, the swifter they flew like arrows. The dew deep, the mist white, with the colour showing in the burning-bush of the garden, on a certain morning a rickshaw drew suddenly up and Tatsuya came in, smiling. Zenpei rose in delight as if he had been lying in wait for him and asked him upstairs. At the sight of him Mitsuyo, she knew not why, shuddered again.
notes: Carriage rendered as rickshaw for Meiji Tokyo kuruma, as in earlier pages; nishikigi given as burning-bush. The final shudder keeps Mitsuyo's bodily intuition rather than explaining it.

payload.say: Drafted p96 keeping the spider thread and Mitsuyo's fretful catalogue intact.

payload.english: From that day Tatsuya's comings and goings at the Miyoshi house came with no more pause than waves breaking on the shore. Between him and Zenpei it was quite as if they were kin. Everyone indoors knew that he was the weighty man in this affair, and with Zenpei to lead them not one of them thought to treat him slightingly. Tatsuya cast his spider's thread as he pleased and gathered them all into his net. So from the lowliest maid to the retired elder above he became the intimate among intimates, until the Miyoshi house and Tatsuya were no longer to be parted. Standing in the midst of it, Mitsuyo alone nursed her anger. Tatsuya grew more distasteful the more she looked at him, she knew not why, and her father who drew so close to him was hateful, her mother who kept no distance was mortifying, her easy elder sister was hateful, her smiling elder brother she could have bitten, and on every side nothing pleased her, on every side nothing pleased her, until at last in the fret that boiled over in her, the workaday maid who bore the brunt of it stood at a loss, tearful and wondering what to do, a strange picture of the world. Mitsuyo waited for Tsunao with a single heart. Knowing nothing of her feeling, Tsunao still did not come home. Alone and melancholy Mitsuyo gazed at the clouds of morning and evening. Her breast, bound to a destination she could not fix, grew ever more painful, and wondering where he might now be and what doing, the mirror she faced showed a worn face, and even that was soon clouded with a sigh.
notes: Took 上の隠居 as the retired senior of the house, set against 末の婢, rather than a named parent; the sense is from the lowest servant to the highest idler.
Kept the doubled 面白くなくて面白くなくて as a plain repetition, and the mirror clouded by a sigh as written, without explaining the sigh.

payload.say: Drafted the reception display and the summons of Mitsuyo.

payload.english: He never looked her way, his mind elsewhere, for rare guests were to come that day, and from early bed Zenpei was astir with preparations: sweep the garden, bring out the cushions, the hand brazier with its ginboya fittings, the Ikkan well bucket tobacco tray, in the alcove his boast, a Tanyu, the set of three scrolls of the Three Evenings poems for all to look at, the flower vase by Soho, mark but the signature, holding the autumn brocade of hill and field, and, with its heart at Tsukushi Bay, on the makie tray of plovers over waves, the stacked incense box in kintame lacquer said to be of Kamakura, set beside the kinuta celadon censer, and in the grip of the silver leaf tongs the brushwood boat parting the mist, its destination known only at the end of the smoke, enough to make one nod and nod again in the heart; to one side, on the rosewood stand inlaid with enamel, the silver hawk figure set out, let that too be counted among the talk, and the gold screen in full color, Korin birds and flowers wrought in relief with all his art; a splendid room, blue mats with Korai edging on which a jewel might be laid without shame, looking out before on the full wabi of the tea garden, a delight for shifting eyes, here is where worth is to be weighed, and, more pleased than any guest to come, his face streaked sideways with soot, the master alone looked round on every side, crying superb.
notes: Kept the reception list vessel by vessel as in the Japanese, including Tanyu, Soho, makie, kintame, kinuta celadon, Korin and Korai edging, without summarizing. Ginboya fitting, the Three Evenings scrolls, and the description of the leaf tongs with brushwood boat and smoke were kept literal though the exact workshop or picture reference is uncertain. Soot smudge kept as the sign of the pleased host inspecting his own display.

payload.english: "Toyo, wipe the go stones clean. Risuke, now, the hand basin, the thread patterned bowls are in the storehouse. The Nankin blue and white clam dishes, shall it be these or shall it be those, Mitsuyo, where is Mitsuyo, Mitsuyo, Mitsuyo." Called out thus, Mitsuyo came forward against her will, and Zenpei rose to outdo himself. "Now today, you see, with Okumura-sama and other important guests, you must come out and pour for us. Change your clothes now and be quick to get ready," he ordered her.
notes: Kept the repeated calling of Mitsuyo and the run of orders as bustle. Thread patterned bowls, hand basin and Nankin clam dishes kept literal; storehouse follows kura. Kept Okumura-sama to hold the rank climbing.

payload.say: Drafted p99-p100 with Mitsuyo sullen in her room and the banquet heard from afar.

payload.english: From the first Mitsuyo wore no pleasant face, and listened as if lending only her ears, until, with her wonted wilfulness showing its force at such a moment, she said, "My stomach aches today, so please excuse me," and rose curtly from her place. That day she never once showed her face outside her room.

Before long the guests came in, for the most part in Western dress and black-bearded, and for a while after they entered the room they gave themselves to hushed and close counsel; then, as they opened out and settled to either side, the dishes carried in were the fruit of Zenshiro's careful knife, and before the exchange of cups was half done merry voices were already rising in laughter. Hearing it from afar, Mitsuyo's eyes brimmed with vexation. That in the hurry of the reception not one soul came to visit her was, to a girl's heart, one grievance more.
notes: I read "shichibu" as "for the most part" rather than a counted seven in ten, and kept it vague as the Japanese is vague about number.
I read "futakawa ni inagaretaru" as the party opening from close counsel and settling to sit on both sides; the syntax leaves the exact movement open.
I keep "black-bearded" with the same "beard" word for the beard motif, though the Japanese here uses髯.

payload.english: Dusk had turned to evening, the silver lights shone full, and when the guests had at last scattered, there remained Tatsuya and Zenpei. With fresh dishes laid in a separate room, the two threw themselves into close talk. Setting down his cup to take breath, Zenpei said, "At this rate you will surely not refuse me. Though the fee for your good offices is small, let it stand at ten thousand yen, and upon success I will present a thousand yen yearly as thanks money. What, you say that to your colleagues and the others who have acted with you, the gentlemen here today, some share of allotment money is also due? That, well, indeed, such payments will have to be made, but in due course I shall consult on that point with my associates and arrange it in one way or another, so let the commission to yourself be fixed for now at just that sum, and first of all to bar the Kunitomo Company's application on its way and get my own before the ministry with all speed is the wise course, and in any case I would ask at once for your exertions toward bringing this matter together, leaving further reward to be settled once the affair is concluded, and I trust there will be no objection to that?"
notes: Zenpei's opening 'kore naraba, anata mo tokou wa gozarimasu mai' is deprecating and elliptical; I take it as pressing the offer while asking him not to refuse it as too small.

I kept 'ginshoku' as 'silver lights' rather than specifying candlesticks or lamps, and 'kan' / 'tsukasa' language as 'the ministry' to keep procedure concrete without importing a term the sentence does not name.

payload.english: Tatsuya shook his head with an amused smile. "Now, what I have to say comes to just this. To be sure, in your way of thinking, if only the forwarding of the papers is hurried through, all else may be left for after, and there is reason enough in what you say, but as to those applications, that it is a case I cannot manage by myself however I try is as I have told you before. The Kunitomo Company's business was at first in my charge, but now the bureau chief has taken it in hand and stands openly as the patron of the Company in all things, so that once the application is ready tomorrow or in two or three days, on the day the Company presents it to the ministry there will be no good way to lie in wait on the road and hinder it. Hence before the matter comes to pass there is nothing for it but to draw that chief into our hands and talk him round into travelling to some distant place. While the chief is not in Tokyo, and from his place of travel holds the Company's application in check from afar so that it is not sent, I shall by my own contrivance make use of the head of the supervisory office, that man with the thick beard who came a while ago, set him to stand in the breach at this juncture, and without putting my hand to either side quietly pull the strings. But for that, should anything go amiss, the careers of we three must be sacrificed for your sake, and that after success would be one thing, but coming after the assignation-house affair you know of, should conduct of this sort be laid bare before society again, it would in truth be a bad business."
notes: Kept 'man with the thick beard' for the supervisory chief to hold the echo with Tatsuya's black beard and the black-bearded guests.

'The careers of we three must be sacrificed for your sake' follows the Japanese closely, but whether Tatsuya means risk undertaken for Zenpei or compensation owed by him is left unsettled in the sentence, and I have kept the risk sense.
'Assignation-house affair' renders the prior待合事件 as a previous scandal that raises the stakes here, without adding explanation beyond the text.

payload.say: Drafted the close bargaining in flat procedural English, keeping speakers unattributed where the text leaves them so.

payload.english: So what I have to ask of you in confidence is this. As I said a while ago, you see, well, whatever happens, I must have your agreement here, and besides that there is one thing more, of a different nature from this present matter, which I must beg you to grant, but that shall be for after. For today, as to the course I spoke of just now, Miyoshi-san, will you not contrive somehow to promise it? Upon success it is three hundred thousand yen, pure profit to be seen as early as tomorrow itself, is it not?
notes: I take the three hundred thousand yen as Tatsuya holding out Zenpei's gain to press him to promise, but the Japanese leaves open whether it names Zenpei's profit or Tatsuya's demand, so I kept wording that does not decide. I kept Miyoshi-san in romanised suffix as the familiarity is part of the pressure.

payload.english: "Indeed, indeed," Zenpei answered, lifting his cup again. "That too is true. To begin with, by some strange fate I came, quite beyond looking for it, upon your acquaintance, and so this consultation has come about. The beginning and the settlement of the matter all lie in your sole exertions, and so in consideration of those exertions..." Here his words failed him a while, then, "Very well. That much I will give."
notes: The referent of that much is left open in the Japanese, whether the ten thousand yen and yearly thanks money of p101 or the three hundred thousand yen just named, so I kept that much flat and did not resolve it.

payload.english: Tatsuya drew his knee forward with a still more amused smile. "Now that you have consented, this Okumura is at ease."

"But," he said, brushing the ash from his cigar, "whatever the result may prove, you will never hereafter raise any objection, will you? We for our part are resolved, should occasion require, to resign our offices together and, as private men together, to take the matter in hand for good."
"Of course, if the matter fails and we gain not a whit of profit...?"
notes: The Japanese gives no narrator tag for p107 and p108, leaving speaker to infer. I leave p107 unattributed as the text does, rather than assigning it to Zenpei.

payload.english: "Very well, we will remit half our expenses for good offices," showing a smile in the eyes, "but if, as we have long purposed, the hour of its accomplishment comes...?"
notes: The smile in the eyes has no stated subject in the Japanese. I render it as a subjectless participle to keep the same degree of not knowing, and leave the question unfinished as the text does.

payload.say: Drafted the bargain riddle and ledger close, keeping the wish vague and the contractual certainly flat.

payload.english: "Then whatever lies within my power, I will meet your wish. Be it a house or a villa, I shall certainly render a fitting thanks besides."
notes: Kept 'certainly' for きっと to hold the flat contractual echo that answers Mitsuyo's 'truly' insistence.

payload.english: "Nay, I receive your great goodwill with gratitude," Tatsuya said, smiling again. "Well then, whatever lies within your power, you will meet my wish, Miyoshi-san, certainly you will," he pressed, as if in jest.

"Now, what might that wish be?" Zenpei edged his knees forward, buoyed by drink. "Well, were I to name it for a start, it would be something like asking to receive what you yourself have fashioned," Tatsuya said, his voice lifting. "Ha! That sounds a riddle with something behind it," Zenpei laughed aloud.
notes: Left 'what you yourself have fashioned' vague as in the Japanese; it points to Mitsuyo only at p130 and must not be clarified here.

payload.english: "Nay, that riddle you shall solve for me another day. First, anew to the fore celebration of this venture," Tatsuya said, offering his cup. Left with none to answer him, Zenpei was already at the hour of sleep.
Things went without hitch, quite as hoped. One item, a slight token, twenty-five thousand yen. That night Tatsuya lodged in Shimbashi, as was his custom.
notes: 'Slight token' renders 薄儀, a euphemism for the cash payment; 'lodged in Shimbashi' keeps the assignation quarter implication without explaining it.

payload.english: Seven

payload.say: Drafted p115 to p117 in high narrative register with the household's grievances and the broken match left as stated.

payload.english: Word that Tsunao had at last come home reached the Miyoshi house through another mouth. Yet he did not readily show his face this way, and Zenpei, worldly-minded as he was, took it greatly amiss. With "he is always despising me, to begin with," uncle and nephew grew by degrees more strained. Mitsuyo's mother, a hater of scholars from of old, was not silent at such a time. Cold by nature at the best of days, such slights were nothing new in Tsunao. He had not come with condolences after the recent fire; the congratulations on the recent birth had come only long after, when the time was near forgotten, and so on and on without end were counted the faults of a Tsunao ignorant of the ways of the world.
notes: Kept the litany of slights as the household's counting, not the narrator's judgment; "ignorant of the ways of the world" for 世情に疎き to keep the worldly register against Tsunao.

payload.english: Unable to bear it, Mitsuyo stole to call on Tsunao in secret. Tsunao was not at home. Mitsuyo waited and waited, as long as the hour allowed. Tsunao never came. Rising with a body ready to weep, she drooped her way home at last, only to learn that Tsunao had called in her absence. Ah, what a want of meeting, she wept in her heart.
notes: Kept the repeated waiting and not-coming unvaried; "what a want of meeting" holds back from naming fate more strongly than 縁のない allows.

payload.english: Within, Zenpei was raging as if afire. At sight of his daughter he raised his voice, "Mitsuyo, the match with Tsunao is broken off. I cannot give you to such a perverse, incomprehensible fellow. Count all promises until now as no more."
notes: Kept 縁 and 約束 as "match" and "promises" without naming Tsunao fiancé, per the open question on how formal the understanding is.

payload.say: Drafted p118 to p123 in flat procedural prose with Tatsuya triumphant and Zenpei attentive.

payload.english: The canvassing over the disposal of the Kijima mine grew fiercer and fiercer between the two sides. The party belonging to the Kunitomo Shōkai answered move with move and yielded nothing, and with other rivals now grown to several besides, the so-called estimated price rose steadily till a figure of 350,000 yen was heard, and as the contest showed no sign of readily ending, even those in charge could no longer manage it, and so it came to the issuing of a single cabinet ordinance. As this ordinance laid down the rules for the lease or disposal of mines, even such applications for disposal as had been made must now be submitted anew under it.
notes: Cabinet ordinance renders kakurei, Official Gazette in p120 renders kanpō; kept as concrete procedure terms without explaining what context will show.

payload.english: It was the day before that ordinance was to appear in the Official Gazette. Tatsuya invited Zenpei, unknown to any other, to the upstairs of a certain machiai, an assignation house, and let him know how pressing matters had become, and told him that thus the last great victory stood once more before his eyes.
notes: Machiai kept in Japanese with gloss, as assignation house used for secret political meeting; see p102 procedure note on machiai affair.

payload.english: "Now, as to that long-standing affair, the Kunitomo party is working as fiercely as we are, so it has become an extraordinary contest on both sides, and after all your long labors up to now, the minister in charge will likely issue a cabinet ordinance about tomorrow, intending to settle victory and defeat at once by it, but even this is a secret within secrets, and besides the minister in charge not a soul in the ministry knows of it."
Sending him a smile full of triumph, as if to say look at me, Tatsuya in high spirits quietly blew out his cigar smoke.
notes: Kept cigar smoke in same wording as p16 to hold calculation pause.

payload.english: "That you should have come to hear of so weighty a design," Miyoshi, who had listened with keen attention, lifted his face and said, "and under what manner of provisions shall the award be decided?"

payload.say: Drafted the cabinet ordinance and draft copy exchange at p124 to p129.

payload.english: "Now, there is nothing particularly difficult about those provisions. The reason for putting out the ordinance is simply this: whatever satisfies every condition laid down in the law shall promptly be granted the disposal, whatever does not shall have its papers rejected all together, and where there are several papers that satisfy the conditions in due form, the first application to arrive shall be adopted. That appears to be the arrangement. payload.say:
Every other note (F1-F3, R1-R3, R5-R11, R13, R16, R17, and the non-gloss parts of R4, R14 and R15) was taken by edit, in the smallest form that did the job, for the reasons given with each edit in the margin.

Declined, with reasons a reader can follow:
- F5 — see the p132 disagreement below; the fragment question is not settled by declining alone.
- R4's parenthetical explanation of Kōrin, R14's 'child's play — as easy as breakfast before morning rice', and R15's 'newly-hatched chick / clip her wings': each would clarify or smooth an image the Japanese leaves as it stands (a style-word, a soliloquy idiom, a bird figure), so only the grammar around those images was changed.
- R18 — its em-dash re-pointing of Zenpei's orders is declined because the house uses an em dash only where the Japanese has ――; the run-together orders and repeated calling of Mitsuyo are the household bustle itself.
- R19 — Zenpei's garbled echo of the allotment-money terms is his incredulous repetition of Tatsuya's proposal in mid-negotiation; recasting it as a tidy direct question would rationalise the procedural talk the reading asks to keep airless.
- R20 as a textual change — the closing fragments and the unstated 'it' already stand as written; the disagreement with F5 is recorded below instead.

Disagreements and unsettled points:
- p14 (F1 against R9's span, though they pull together): faithful — 国色 is the daughter alone; readable — 'in his breast' is not English. Choice: both points taken in one line, 'she a peerless beauty' and 'to himself'. The reading settles it; not sent up.
- p28 (R12): faithful — Zenpei's threefold 'lies' must echo Mitsuyo's 'truly' unvaried; readable — English cannot laugh a lie. Choice: 'shall I laugh in lies, lies, lies?', keeping the repetition and giving the verb an object it can govern. Settled by the repetition motif; not sent up.
- p48 (R14): faithful — 朝飯前 is Tatsuya's brisk sporting idiom and must stay visible; readable — 'as easy as breakfast' alone is a calque. Choice: the idiom kept, hyphen supplied, explanatory expansion declined. The soliloquy's untroubled sporting voice settles it; not sent up.
- p132 (F5 against R20): faithful — 明日は誰が身の is a hanging fragment and 'shall it fall' completes it; readable — a bare fragment reads as dropped words, not withholding. Choice: the present 'Tomorrow, upon whom shall it fall' stands, with what falls still unnamed. The reading demands the withholding but does not settle whether English may supply the verb, and the final line is where being wrong matters most — sent up to the editor.
- p77-p78 (F4): the source prints 鋼雄 twice for 綱雄. Choice: English keeps 'Tsunao' and the variant is flagged, not silently absorbed — sent up for a check against the 1895 text.

Nothing in this part showed that an earlier part should be re-read: who anyone is and what the repeated words mean here match the house's understanding, apart from the name-variant flag above.

House log: The desk took the readers' corrections on the beauty's reference, the introduction at p43, the consistent 'Uncle', Zenpei's laughter, the rank-title and the closing catalogue of the mine, while refusing every change that would gloss, vary or complete what the text deliberately leaves strange, repeated or unresolved.

payload.body: Tanyu is the Kano-school painter Kano Tanyu, whose work was a standard boast in a formal alcove. Soho names a vase-maker prized for tea flower-vases. The Three Evenings are three celebrated autumn-verse topics, here as a set of three scrolls.

payload.body: Kinuta is a type of grey-green celadon, named after stone beaters for cloth. Kintame is a gold-rich lacquer finish, and makie is lacquer sprinkled with gold or silver powder, here plovers over waves.

chapter_summaries.0: Part One at Komatsu spa in autumn decline. Tatsuya, ministry secretary on sick leave, hears koto and singing in annex, questions maid, is shown best room for rank and beard. He sees fat laughing old man at railing, walks to Ogi lake bower, glimpses maiden on second floor and takes her for singer, then meets her full beauty in bath corridor. Old man is Miyoshi Zenpei with daughter Mitsuyo; bath talk makes them intimates; Tatsuya learns names and wealth and privately marks Mitsuyo as beautiful prey and Zenpei as not to be let escape.

hard_spots.why_hard: Long tide-like Meiji landscape sentences with kanbun colouring (堆藍前にあり凝黛後にあり, 煙波縹緲, 漁唱菱歌) and bird/plant names. Do not prune into efficient setting; luxuriance is the world Tatsuya exploits and the innocent cover for pursuit. Keep periodic rhythm without ennobling into Victorian purple.

Mitsuyo 真実に six times, Zenpei mocks back 嘘に six times. Must stay repetitive and childish, not varied for elegance. Later bargaining echoes with きっと/ようございます certainty over her — preserve echo, do not smooth.

Reception vessels named vessel by vessel: 銀穂屋付き手炉, 一閑釣瓶煙草盆, 探幽, 三夕三幅対, 宗甫花入, 蒔絵盆, 金溜塗重香合, 碪手青磁香炉, 七宝紫檀卓, 銀蒼鷹置物, 光琳金屏風. Social satire and circumstantial density at once. Needs identification plus material specificity; do not summarise away. Ruby/old names need glossing in margin.

願書, 払い下げ, 借区, 閣令, 官報, 周旋料, 割賦金, 謝金, 待合事件. Corruption is concrete sequence of applications, first-filing rule, travel alibis. Must remain precise and slightly airless; do not turn into vague bribery atmosphere. 待合事件 (assignation scandal) is prior disgrace raising stakes — annotate.
Tsunao printed once as 鋼雄 for 綱雄. Almost certainly press/transcription slip. Do not invent character difference; normalise in English to Tsunao and note for editor to check 1895 Taiyo text.

Tatsuya ore soliloquy (兵は神速, こん粉微塵) must sound exuberant/comic, not brooding; demand お貰い申しましたよ is brutal plain; close われはこの後のことを知らず with double rhetorical questions must not name wife or philosopher. English pronouns/connectives must keep knowing-and-not-knowing.

motifs.english: Keep same English word each time: 'beard' (with black/thick where source adds). Do not vary to whiskers/moustache. It marks fashionable manhood and trips the comedy when Mitsuyo insults Tsunao's beard and remembers Tatsuya's.
motifs.why: Admired splendid beard, accidental insult, returning official with thick side-whiskers. Deliberate echo of worldly masculinity.

motifs.english: Keep 'Hotei' with gloss once (squat laughing god), then repeat Hotei bulk/laugh. Keep 'laugh' verb repeated for Zenpei rather than varying to chuckle/guffaw.
motifs.why: Softens everything Zenpei does until it does not; warmth that makes treating daughter as asset possible.

motifs.english: Keep 'cigar smoke' / 'puffed smoke' language steady. Smoke pauses mark calculation admiring its own plan.
motifs.why: Appetite taking a pause. Punctuates Tatsuya scheming and Zenpei self-satisfaction; links pleasure to plotting.

motifs.english: Keep Mitsuyo's 'truly, truly, truly...' unvaried and excessive; keep Zenpei's mocking 'lies, lies...' parallel. Later keep bargaining 'certainly / without fail / promise' flat and repeated to let horror rhyme.
motifs.why: Childish insistence becomes contractual certainty. Do not elegant-vary; structure depends on echo.

motifs.english: Keep 'voice' and 'listen' wording: singing voice, listening ear, still listening. Do not resolve singer early; preserve inference.
motifs.motif: music behind the screen and listening
motifs.why: Mitsuyo first exists as sound; Tatsuya at lake still listening back to shoji. Governs desire as overhearing and pursuit as innocent aesthetic attention.

narration.english_tense: Past as default for narrative action; preserve scenic present participles only where Japanese scenic period invites sustained tableau, without flipping whole story into historic present. Dialogue past/present as spoken. Soliloquy in vivid present.
narration.frame: Third-person impersonal lyrical narrator with free access to private thought and soliloquy, but who withdraws at the end into professed ignorance. Linear seasonal movement autumn spa to autumn Tokyo with accelerated intrigue and rumoured aftermath.
narration.narrator: Elevated Meiji literary narrator, never judging villain directly; moral shown by juxtaposition of surface charm and private counting. Closes with われ (I) refusing knowledge.
narration.tense_habits: Classical-literary auxiliaries (なり, ぬ, たり, けり, ごとし) giving completed poetic past; scenery in sustained periodic present-like tableau; dialogue in Meiji colloquial -ます/-だ. Shifts freely without signalling interior vs exterior.
timeline: Autumn: Tatsuya convalescing at Komatsu Umeya inn meets singing, Zenpei and Mitsuyo; walks, bath familiarity, learns names and wealth (p2-p16).
Next day(s): Go games, Zenpei-Mitsuyo pillow comedy, walk with Mitsuyo, Tsunao arrival, quarrel, Tsunao silent departure (p19-p83).
Immediate return to Tokyo: Zenpei telegrams over Kijima mine tip, Mitsuyo waits for Tsunao, Tatsuya becomes household intimate and spider (p85-p96).
Banquet and private bargain: commission/annual thanks-money, riddle of Mitsuyo, cabinet-order draft for first-filing win and demand of Mitsuyo (p97-p130).
Aftermath withheld: rumour of Tatsuya wife and philosopher recluse, seasonal close (p132).

part_summaries.summary: Part One at Komatsu spa in autumn decline. Tatsuya, ministry secretary on sick leave, hears koto and singing in annex, questions maid, is shown best room for rank and beard. He sees fat laughing old man at railing, walks to Ogi lake bower, glimpses maiden on second floor and takes her for singer, then meets her full beauty in bath corridor. Old man is Miyoshi Zenpei with daughter Mitsuyo; bath talk makes them intimates; Tatsuya learns names and wealth and privately marks Mitsuyo as beautiful prey and Zenpei as not to be let escape.

Part Two in Zenpei rooms. After half-day go, Zenpei praises Tatsuya rank and talent and disparages Tsunao; Mitsuyo defends Tsunao as younger, refined, calm, high-spirited. Teasing about Tsunao visit turns into father-daughter pillow comedy with six-times truly tantrum, threats to break incense box and spoil haori, seized air-pillow. Zenpei offers tea, Mitsuyo goes to bath. Establishes indulgence as household language and Tsunao as expected ally.

Part Three morning walk to lake shore. Tatsuya presses Mitsuyo to walk, shifts through light talk and confesses listening to her koto; she deflects to scenery. Lush lake tableau. On return they meet Zenpei bringing stranger Tojo Tsunao; Mitsuyo runs alive to him, mocks his beard then catches Tatsuya black beard and laughs apology. Introductions chill: Tsunao arrogant, Tatsuya inwardly hostile; Zenpei alone imagines mutual respect. Four walk back, Mitsuyo childishly runs ahead for souvenir.

Part Four split scene. Tatsuya alone in ore voice vows to crush Tojo to powder, take Mitsuyo at one blow, hook father to cover debts, speed is everything, summons Zenpei via maid. Intercut: Zenpei urges Tsunao to bend and associate; Tsunao refuses as floating thin man; Mitsuyo agrees she dislikes Tatsuya; Zenpei defends sociability; quarrel, Tatsuya summons arrives, Zenpei storms out, Mitsuyo begs Tsunao to bend and stay by her, Tsunao will not bend self, talks of leaving, tender wavering then refusal; country singing and masseur mark time. Tsunao leaves without farewell to either, leaving letter; car sound fades.

Part Five return. Zenpei returns calling for Tsunao, learns flight, forgets it for three telegrams on Kijima coal mine tip from Tatsuya: cheap at 200,000, worth 500,000, quality beyond Miike, naval contracts. Mitsuyo bored and uncomforted asks to go home; Zenpei plans hasty Tokyo return for arrangements. Corridor meeting with Tatsuya, Mitsuyo turns away; men whisper laugh; Tatsuya sends regards to Tsunao. Mine displaces daughter in attention.

Part Six in Tokyo autumn. Mitsuyo rushes to Tsunao who has not returned; Zenpei races east-west in consultations; Tatsuya becomes daily intimate, spider thread over whole house from maid to retiree while Mitsuyo alone grows hostile and waits gaunt for Tsunao. Great reception prepared vessel by vessel for Tatsuya and important guests; Mitsuyo pleads bellyache and hides weeping unvisited. After guests leave, private bargain: 10,000 handling plus 1,000 yearly thanks-money, shares to colleagues, blocking Kunitomo application via bureau chief travel and supervisor front, risk of exposure after machiai scandal; Zenpei agrees, Tatsuya presses promise of anything in his power and riddles at what Zenpei has made. Night payment hint 25,000 yen; Tatsuya stays at Shimbashi as usual.

Part Seven break and final trap. Tsunao return rumoured but does not visit; Zenpei resents contempt, mother counts scholar slights; Mitsuyo secretly visits absent Tsunao then finds he came in her absence. Zenpei in rage declares Mitsuyo-Tsunao understanding broken. Mining race intensifies to 350,000 yen estimates, cabinet ordinance to decide by conditions and first filing. Tatsuya lures Zenpei to secret assignation upstairs, reveals draft ordinance obtained, promises certain flag if paper filed instantly on publication, demands reward: Mitsuyo herself — O-morai moshimashita. Narrator withdraws: does not know aftermath; Tatsuya said to have taken wife — who?; someone cast trouble away for half-life philosophy — who?; autumn wind over Ogi and paulownia; whose turn tomorrow.

bible.say: Charm must stay charming and procedure stay procedural; do not rescue Tsunao into heroism, do not judge Tatsuya early, do not resolve the withheld ending.

style_sheet.annotation_density: Moderate: gloss spa, rank/title, mine system, vessels and ordinance terms, assignation-house and Shimbashi usage, Hotei and Kōrin references. Never annotate what context supplies; never use note to moralise or resolve ending.
style_sheet.author_voice: Three movements: lush periodic scenery (long tide-like sentences, autumn plants, water, light) kept lush but readable; sharp colloquial dialogue where each speaker breaks register; flat concrete procedure for bribes and papers. Keep movement audible; do not flatten into uniform fluent novel prose. Avoid Berman tidying: no rationalised syntax, no clarified subjects, no ennobled diction, no varied synonyms for deliberate repeats.
style_sheet.honorifics_and_names: Japanese order surname-given (Miyoshi Zenpei, Okumura Tatsuya) with macrons (Tōjō Tsunao, Miyoshi Mitsuyo) on first use; thereafter surname or given as Japanese does. Keep -san / -sama / -sama vs -san difference in romanised suffix because rank-climbing and intimacy live in it; explain once. Keep Sensei only if text uses 先生 (it does not; do not import). Servant/master terms (旦那-like 亭主, お方様) rendered to show deference without Victorianism.
style_sheet.keep_in_japanese: Vessel and art terms with gloss once then English:探幽 (Tan'yū school painting), 仁清香合 (Ninsei incense box), 碪手青磁 (kinuta celadon), 光琳風 (Kōrin style). Keep realia: 梅屋 (Umeya), 停車場 spelling flavour, 待合 (assignation house), 官報 (Official Gazette), 閣令 (cabinet ordinance) with brief note. Keep cigar as 葉巻/シガー signal.
style_sheet.quotation: Japanese binds dialogue in narrative without consistent quotes; use English double quotes for direct speech, single for thought-as-utterance where needed. Keep unattributed turns unattributed where Japanese leaves speaker to infer; do not add tags to tidy.
style_sheet.register: Narrative high-literary but not archaic: plain strong English with periodic length for scenery. Dialogue colloquial Meiji Tokyo: Zenpei bluff and familiar, Mitsuyo girlish polite with prolongation and pout, Tsunao stiff formal, Tatsuya accommodating chameleon. Soliloquy coarse ore energy, comic and brisk, not Gothic.
style_sheet.ruby_and_italics: Use italics for Japanese retentions (-san/-sama, vessel names, realia) on first setting and sparingly after. Render ruby glosses (笆まがき, 媚こぶる etc.) only where reading changes sense; otherwise silent. Do not italicise repeated motif English words.
